Since I havent posted much about whats been going on in my nation the last in game months, heres a summary:

Warning: big text post lol I wasnt even trying to do this

Tl, dr; protest movement in Marqana province, anti corruption campaign so far, Islamic university enrollment is up, establishment of the Ministry of Enjoining Good and Forbidding evil but its not morality police as much as it is an Islamic law inspection group and social service assistance group, and the various religions of the country have their biggest holiday and festival celebrations in Baladullahan history

[spoiler=Whats goin on]

[b]Occupy Baladullah Movement[/b]

After snap elections of July 2026, in which the ruling NSF coalition saw massive gains throughout the country, the opposition has claimed these elections were rigged. A few rounds of protests, mainly in the opposition stronghold province of Marqana and its capital city, Maghlaba, saw turnouts of tens to hundreds of thousands of people, some rioting, and hundreds of arrests. 

In October, the official investigation into allegations of voter fraud and tampering concluded there were some glitches and errors, but no intentional rigging or fraud of any kind. This reignited protests in Marqana, and the Citizens for Change movement emerged, led by a former regional representative of Marqana named Ali Qarmandi. 

Their demands are for an opposition-coalition sponsored probe into the July elections, the release of the 150 or so people still in jail since the summer protests, an opposition-led investigation into corruption, and for the HSI to reverse its decision to consider itself the vanguard of the social Islamic revolution, as this is seen as an indication that the HSI-led NSF coalition is trying to take power permanently. 

After a few more protest groups and some NGOs joined up with Citizens for Change, it began calling itself Occupy Baladullah in late November 2026, and also did indeed begin occupying parks, government buildings, central squares in towns and cities around Marqana, and has set up a Peoples Assembly in Maghlaba since December 2, 2026. The government is currently engaged in negotiations with this movements leaders to resolve the issues they have brought up. 

Daily protests have also been going on in Maghlaba and other cities and towns in Marqana, most of them have been peaceful, but a massive riot took place in the Al-Ahrar neighborhood of Maghlaba from October 30 to November 1 after police fired hundreds of canisters of tear gas at peaceful protesters in just a few minutes and began beating and attacking them for no apparent reason. 150 people were wounded, and 300 arrested and taken into custody with no charges. The riots destroyed most of the neighborhood, and left 15 people dead including 8 police officers. 

On November 2, Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi fired the police chief of Maghlaba and also 30 officers involved in the brutal suppression of the incident, and established a joint committee with the opposition alliance to investigate that incident and other reported incidents of police brutality. This is still underway, but already 15 police officers have been sentenced to 5 to 25 years in prison, the National Police of Baladullah has paid 15 million dirhams to the protesters and their families affected by the October 30 terror, and Citizens for Change has been given the right to establish a police monitoring organization in Marqana. 

[b]Anti Corruption Efforts Achieve Moderate Success[/b]

Since the launch of the anti-corruption drive last summer, 50 people have been arrested and sentenced to death for corruption charges related to bribery, embezzlement, and blackmail, while another 100 have been sentenced to life in jail. These include 75 of the top 100 wealthiest people in the country, and half of them are from ruling coalition parties. 

However, the opposition claims that 15 of the people sentenced to death are only guilty of being staunch opponents of the government, while 20 sentenced to life in jail are in the same boat. The government denies these charges.

[b]Islamic Education and Activism[/b]

More people enrolled in Islamic universities focused on jurisprudence (Fiqh), community outreach and sharing the message of true Islam (dawah), and the implementation of Islamic law (shariah) in 2026 than the previous 5 years. There are now an estimated 125 universities that only teach Islamic subjects or from an  exclusively Islamic perspective, up from 85 five years ago, and the fall 2026 semester saw their total enrollment number go to 115,000 people, up from 95,000 in the spring 2026 semester. In general, of the 25,000 universities of colleges in Baladullah, some 15,000 of them now teach all Islamic subjects listed above. 

The government also recently established the Ministry of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil, in November 2026, whose purpose is to make sure everyone is paying zakat and jizyah, that no establishments are selling drugs or alcohol, advising people to dress and act modestly, and also helping to run volunteer programs, social programs, and to find out who is in need of any assistance in financial, religious, or social  matters and then connecting them to the appropriate services. The ministry does not enforce dress code, however, nor does it have the ability to force anyone to do anything or to arrest people. Members (called guardians) can call the police if they find any place is selling drugs or alcohol, but thats it.

[b]Jewish, Christian, Druze, and Zoroastrian Festivals See Record Turnouts, Including By Interested Muslims[/b]

Throughout the year, the religious communities of the country have many holidays, festivals, and celebrations, all of which are constitutionally protected and may be fully and openly practiced. 2026 saw the greatest total participation in these events of any year in Baladullahan history, an event celebrated by the government, and the Sultan, Grand Shaykh of the country, and other Islamic figures and average Muslim citizens took part in conversations and feasts during these holidays with their fellow non-Muslim citizens. 

In particular, Hanukkah 2026 saw a large menorah placed in the Garden of Peace (Jannah us-Salaam) in the Jewish dominant neighborhood of Michpeachea in southeast Medinah al-Islam. There were hundreds of people there every night to see the lighting of the large torch candles, and to sing Jewish songs and recite Torah verses. Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi and top Islamic scholars in the nation observed these events and spoke on the importance of preserving the multi religious and multicultural culture of Baladullah, and how Allah is the same God for everyone and He loves justice and devotion to Him.
[/spoiler]
